stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacist is asked to begin collaboratively managing a walk-in who says her physician mentioned that the pharmacy could help with her blood pressure. Nothing is in writing and the pharmacist has had no contact with the physician. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: She is a collaborative patient because her own physician suggested it.
She is a collaborative patient because she has presented herself for the service.
The supervising physician must assess her and include a diagnosis on referral.
She becomes a collaborative patient once the pharmacist records the conversation.
In this setting she must be notified of and must consent to the services.

explanation.core_reasoning: Statutory eligibility is fixed at s. 24B1/2(a) of M.G.L. c. 112: a patient must be REFERRED to the pharmacist by the supervising physician for the purpose of receiving collaborative services. The supervising physician shall assess the patient and include a diagnosis when referring, and in the retail drug business setting the patient shall be notified of and shall consent to the services.

choice_analysis.A: A remark to the patient is not a referral to the pharmacist.
choice_analysis.B: Presenting for a service does not make a person a collaborative patient.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: assessment and a diagnosis are part of the referral.
choice_analysis.D: A unilateral note by the pharmacist does not create the referral.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: notice and consent are required in the retail setting.

related_facts: Individual referral and consent must be recorded by both professionals
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates treat the patient's own account of what a physician said as the referral itself.

reasoning_steps: Ask whether a referral running from physician to pharmacist exists
Check that the referral carries an assessment and a diagnosis
Apply the retail-setting notice and consent requirement
